lessonActivities.title: Reported Questions: Word Order Changes ❓
lessonActivities.content:
Ready for the next level? ❓ Reporting questions requires a special change: the word order becomes like a statement, not a question!

Formation: [Subject] + asked/wanted to know + [question word/if] + [subject + verb in backshifted tense]. Example: 'Where do you live?' → She asked where I lived.

Question TypeDirect SpeechReported StructureKey Change
Wh- Question'What is your name?'She asked what my name was.Keep question word; statement order
Yes/No Question'Are you tired?'He asked if I was tired.Add 'if/whether'; statement order
Present Simple Q'Do you like coffee?'She asked if I liked coffee.Remove 'do/does'; backshift verb
Present Continuous Q'Are you working?'He asked if I was working.Invert subject/verb back; backshift

Fun fact: 'Whether' is a more formal alternative to 'if' in reported yes/no questions! ✨

When to use: If the original was a question, use asked/wanted to know + statement word order. Never use question marks in reported questions!
examples: At a specific time: 'When are you leaving?' → She asked when I was leaving.
Yes/No focus: 'Do you understand?' → He asked if I understood.
Question form: 'Why were you crying?' → She asked why I had been crying.
functions: Converting direct questions to reported form
lessonActivities.tips: When to use: If the original was a question, use asked/wanted to know + statement word order. Never use question marks in reported questions!

lessonActivities.title: Orders, Requests & Advice: Using the Infinitive 📋
lessonActivities.content:
Let's master the full picture! 📋 Knowing how to report orders, requests, and advice completes your control of indirect speech. These use the infinitive!

Formation for Orders/Requests: [Subject] + told/asked + [person] + (not) to + base verb. Example: 'Close the door!' → She told me to close the door.

Formation for Advice/Suggestions: [Subject] + advised/suggested + [person] + (not) to + base verb OR that + clause. Example: 'You should rest' → He advised me to rest.

Direct TypeReporting VerbStructure PatternExample
Ordertold / orderedtold + person + to + verb'Sit down!' → He told me to sit down.
Negative Ordertold / warnedtold + person + not to + verb'Don't touch!' → She told me not to touch.
Polite Requestasked / requestedasked + person + to + verb'Could you help?' → He asked me to help.
Adviceadvised / suggestedadvised + person + to + verb'You should rest' → She advised me to rest.

Fun fact: 'Suggest' can also take 'that + subject + (should) + verb'! 'She suggested that I (should) study.' 🎓

Remember: For orders/requests, use told/asked + to + verb. For advice, advised/suggested + to + verb OR that + clause.
examples: Negative statement: 'Don't be late!' → She told me not to be late.
Yes/No request: 'Could you pass the salt?' → He asked me to pass the salt.
Wh-request: 'Please explain the rule.' → She asked him to explain the rule.
Short answer: 'Will you help?' → She asked if I would help.
lessonActivities.tips: Remember: For orders/requests, use told/asked + to + verb. For advice, advised/suggested + to + verb OR that + clause.

lessonActivities.title: Modal Verbs in Indirect Speech: What Changes? 🔑
lessonActivities.content:
Here's a crucial rule! 🔑 When you report speech with modal verbs, some change and some don't! This trips up many learners.

The Rule: After a past reporting verb, will→would, can→could, may→might, must→had to. But might/could/would/should/ought to stay the same! Example: 'I must go' → He said he had to go.

Modal in DirectMeaningReported FormExample
willfuture intentionwould'I'll help' → She said she would help.
canability/permissioncould'I can swim' → He said he could swim.
maypossibility/permissionmight'It may rain' → She said it might rain.
mustobligationhad to'I must study' → He said he had to study.
shouldadvice (NO CHANGE)should'You should rest' → She said I should rest.

Fun fact: 'Must' for logical deduction ('He must be tired') often stays 'must' in reported speech! 🤔

Never forget: Modals of deduction (must/can't) and advice (should) often don't change. Modals of future/ability/permission usually do!
examples: With 'will': 'I will call' → She said she would call.
With 'can': 'I can help' → He said he could help.
With 'must': 'I must leave' → She said she had to leave.
No change: 'You should try' → He said I should try.
functions: Identifying which modals change in reported speech
lessonActivities.tips: Never forget: Modals of deduction (must/can't) and advice (should) often don't change. Modals of future/ability/permission usually do!

lessonActivities.title: Contrast: Reported Statements vs. Questions vs. Requests 🔄
lessonActivities.content:
Here's where it gets interesting! 🔄 Many learners confuse reported statements, questions, and requests. Let's clarify:

FeatureReported StatementReported QuestionReported Request
Reporting Verbsaid/told/explainedasked/wanted to knowasked/told/advised
Structurethat + clauseif/whether/wh- + statement orderperson + (not) to + verb
ExampleHe said that he was tired.She asked if I was tired.He told me to rest.
PunctuationPeriodPeriod (not ?)Period

The secret: Look at the original speech type. Statement? → that-clause. Question? → if/wh- + statement. Order/Request? → to + verb.

Common mistake: 'She asked me that I was tired' × → 'She asked if I was tired' ✓

Fun fact: Native speakers often drop 'that' in statements but never in questions—clarity matters! 💬

Pro tip: Look for the original speech type first. Then choose the correct reporting structure.
examples: Statement example: 'I like coffee.' → He said he liked coffee.
Question example: 'Do you like coffee?' → He asked if I liked coffee.
Request example: 'Please make coffee.' → He asked me to make coffee.
Wrong vs Right: 'She asked that I was tired' × → 'She asked if I was tired' ✓
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: Look for the original speech type first. Then choose the correct reporting structure.

lessonActivities.title: Advanced: Reported Questions with Complex Tenses ⏳
lessonActivities.content:
Ready for the next level? ⏳ Reporting questions with complex tenses requires careful backshift and word order changes.

Formation: [Subject] + asked + [question word/if] + [subject + backshifted complex verb]. Example: 'Have you been waiting?' → She asked if I had been waiting.

Use this when:

Direct QuestionReported QuestionBackshift PatternExample
Present Perfect Qasked + if + had + past participlehave/has → had'Have you seen it?' → She asked if I had seen it.
Present Perfect Continuous Qasked + if + had been + -inghave been → had been'Have you been waiting?' → He asked if I had been waiting.
Past Simple Qasked + wh- + had + past participledid → had (optional)'Where did you go?' → She asked where I had gone.
Future Questionasked + if + would + verbwill → would'Will you come?' → He asked if I would come.

Fun fact: Past Simple questions can keep simple past or backshift to past perfect—both are acceptable! 🎯

When to use: If you want to emphasize the sequence of past events, use past perfect. For general past reference, simple past is fine.
examples: At a specific time: 'When had you arrived?' → She asked when I had arrived.
Duration focus: 'How long have you been studying?' → He asked how long I had been studying.
Interrupted action: 'What were you doing when...?' → She asked what I had been doing when...
functions: Reporting questions with perfect and continuous tenses
Choosing between past simple and past perfect in reported questions
lessonActivities.tips: When to use: If you want to emphasize the sequence of past events, use past perfect. For general past reference, simple past is fine.

lessonActivities.title: Negative Requests & Orders in Indirect Speech ❌
lessonActivities.content:
Let's master the full picture! ❌ Knowing how to report negative requests and orders completes your control of indirect speech with infinitives.

Negative Formation: [Subject] + told/asked + [person] + not to + base verb. Example: 'Don't be late!' → She told me not to be late.

Direct NegativeStructure PatternReported FormKey Note
Negative OrderDon't + verb!told + person + not to + verb'Not' comes before 'to'
Negative RequestPlease don't + verbasked + person + not to + verbPolite verb: asked
Negative AdviceYou shouldn't + verbadvised + person + not to + verbOr: advised that + subject + shouldn't
Negative WarningBe careful not to...warned + person + not to + verbStronger than 'asked'

Fun fact: 'Not' always comes immediately before 'to' in negative infinitives—never 'to not'! 🚫

Common mistake: 'She told me to not worry' × → 'She told me not to worry' ✓

Remember: In negative infinitives, not goes before to: not to worry, not to be late, not to forget.
examples: Negative statement: 'Don't touch that!' → He told me not to touch that.
Yes/No request: 'Please don't tell anyone.' → She asked me not to tell anyone.
Wh-request: 'Don't forget to call.' → He reminded me not to forget to call.
Short answer: 'Should I worry?' → She advised me not to worry.
lessonActivities.tips: Remember: In negative infinitives, not goes before to: not to worry, not to be late, not to forget.

lessonActivities.title: Indirect Speech with Time Clauses 🕐
lessonActivities.content:
Here's a crucial rule! 🕐 When you use time clauses in reported speech like [when/before/after/while], the tense in the time clause may not backshift!

The Rule: In reported speech, time clauses often keep their original tense even when the main clause backshifts. Example: 'I'll call when I arrive' → She said she would call when she arrived.

Time StarterDirect SpeechReported SpeechTense in Time Clause
when'I'll call when I arrive.'She said she would call when she arrived.Present → Past (backshift)
before'Finish before you leave.'He told me to finish before I left.Present → Past (backshift)
after'I'll call after I've eaten.'She said she would call after she had eaten.Present Perfect → Past Perfect
while'Don't talk while I'm speaking.'He told me not to talk while he was speaking.Present Continuous → Past Continuous

Common mistake: 'She said she would call when she will arrive' × → 'She said she would call when she arrived' ✓

Fun fact: Time clauses follow the same backshift rules as the main clause—just apply them separately! 🔄

Never forget: After [time words], backshift the tense just like in the main clause. Main clause = [tense], time clause = [backshifted tense].
examples: With 'when': 'I'll call when I arrive.' → She said she would call when she arrived.
With 'before': 'Finish before you leave.' → He told me to finish before I left.
With 'after': 'I'll call after I've eaten.' → She said she would call after she had eaten.
Combined clauses: 'When I finish, I'll call.' → He said that when he finished, he would call.
functions: Linking actions in time sequences in reported speech
Applying backshift rules to time clauses correctly
lessonActivities.tips: Never forget: After [time words], backshift the tense just like in the main clause. Main clause = [tense], time clause = [backshifted tense].

lessonActivities.title: Mastery: Advanced Indirect Speech Nuances 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
You've come so far! 🎯 Let's tackle the advanced nuances that separate good from great in indirect speech.

Special Case 1: Mixed Reporting

Sometimes one sentence reports multiple speech types. Example: 'Can you help me because I'm tired?' → She asked if I could help her because she was tired.

Special Case 2: Formal vs. Informal Register

In formal contexts, use precise reporting verbs and full structures. In casual speech, simplify. Formal: 'He inquired whether I would be available.' Casual: 'He asked if I'd be free.'

Context / RegisterPreferred FormRhetorical EffectExemplar
Casual SpeechDropped 'that', contractionsNatural, conversationalHe said he'd call later.
Formal WritingFull structures, precise verbsProfessional, preciseHe stated that he would contact me subsequently.
Academic ReportingPassive voice, hedgingObjective, cautiousIt was reported that the data appeared to support the hypothesis.

Mastery checklist: ✓ Identify speech type ✓ Choose appropriate reporting verb ✓ Apply correct structure ✓ Adjust for register ✓ Check time/place expressions

Fun fact: Native speakers often mix rules in casual speech—focus on clarity first! 💬

Master level: In formal writing, be consistent with structures. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!
examples: Formal context: 'The experiment proves the hypothesis.' → The researcher stated that the experiment proves the hypothesis.
Mixed speech: 'Can you help because I'm busy?' → She asked if I could help because she was busy.
Idiomatic usage: 'It's raining cats and dogs!' → She exclaimed that it was raining heavily.
Academic writing: 'The results indicate a correlation.' → The paper states that the results indicate a correlation.
functions: Using indirect speech in sophisticated ways
Adapting to different registers and contexts
Handling mixed speech types and complex sentences
lessonActivities.tips: Master level: In formal writing, be consistent with structures. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!

writingActivities.question: Convert these direct questions into reported questions: 'Where do you live?' and 'Are you coming tomorrow?'
writingActivities.hint: Use asked + question word (or 'if' for yes/no questions) + subject + backshifted verb. Example: She asked me where I lived.
sentenceStarters: She asked me where...
He wanted to know if...

writingActivities.question: Report this polite request: 'Could you please help me with my homework?'
writingActivities.hint: Use asked + me + to + verb for polite requests. Example: She asked me to help her with her homework.
sentenceStarters: She asked me to...
He requested that I...

writingActivities.question: Tell a short story about what your teacher ordered the class to do. Use reported speech with infinitives at least twice.
writingActivities.hint: Begin with 'The teacher told us to...'. Add details with not to for negative orders.
sentenceStarters: First, the teacher told us to...
Then, she ordered us not to...

writingActivities.question: Describe a conversation where someone asked you a question and gave you advice. Use reported speech for both.
writingActivities.hint: Remember: asked + if/wh- for questions, advised + to + verb for advice. Example: She asked if I was tired and advised me to rest.
sentenceStarters: She asked me if... and advised me to...
He wanted to know... and suggested that I...

writingActivities.question: Compare what two different people asked you using reported questions. Show how their questions differed.
writingActivities.hint: Use however/although to show contrast between their questions. Add similarly/both if they asked similar things.
sentenceStarters: Both John and Mary asked if..., but John also wanted to know...
While Sarah asked where..., Tom inquired whether...

writingActivities.question: Write a paragraph reporting a series of requests you received. Use cause-effect markers to explain why each request was made.
writingActivities.hint: Start with the cause: because/since/as. Then show the request: asked me to.
sentenceStarters: Because it was late, she asked me to...
Since the project was urgent, he told me to...

writingActivities.question: Express an opinion about a rule. Report what someone asked you about it, then give your view.
writingActivities.hint: State your view with I believe/In my opinion. Support it with for example/this is because. Report questions with asked if/whether.
sentenceStarters: In my opinion,... because my teacher asked if...
I believe that... as my colleague inquired whether...

writingActivities.question: Describe a hypothetical situation using reported conditional questions. Include what someone asked you would happen if a condition were met.
writingActivities.hint: Use asked what would happen if + past simple in reported form. Example: She asked what would happen if it rained.
sentenceStarters: She asked what would happen if...
He wanted to know whether I would... if...

writingActivities.question: Report a complex conversation involving a question, an order, and a piece of advice. Show mastery by using correct structures for each.
writingActivities.hint: This requires 3 different structures: asked + if/wh- for questions, told + to + verb for orders, advised + to + verb for advice. Pay attention to pronoun shifts.
sentenceStarters: Although she asked..., he told her to...
When I asked..., she advised me to...

writingActivities.question: Write a formal email summarizing a meeting. Use reported speech to convey questions colleagues asked and requests they made, with hedging language and polite conclusions.
writingActivities.hint: Maintain formal register: avoid contractions, use passive voice/formal connectors, end with polite closing. Report speech with inquired/requested/suggested.
sentenceStarters: It was inquired whether...
One colleague requested that, given the circumstances...

gameActivities.question: Select the correct reported form for this question:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Do you like coffee?' → Reported: She asked ____.
gameActivities.hint: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether' + statement word order + backshifted verb.

gameActivities.question: Choose the appropriate reporting verb for this request:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Please close the window.' → Reported: She ____ me to close the window.
gameActivities.hint: Polite requests use 'asked + person + to + verb'. Orders use 'told'.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct word order for this reported question:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Where is the station?' → Reported: He asked ____.
gameActivities.hint: Reported questions use statement word order: question word + subject + verb.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct modal transformation:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I can swim 500 meters.' → Reported: He said he ____ swim 500 meters.
gameActivities.hint: 'Can' changes to 'could' in reported speech when the reporting verb is past.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct form for this negative request:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Don't be late!' → Reported: She told me ____.
gameActivities.hint: Negative orders: 'told + person + not to + base verb'.

gameActivities.question: Which modal verb does NOT change in reported speech?
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'You should study.' → Reported: She said I ____ study.
gameActivities.hint: Modal verbs of advice (should, ought to) and some modals (might, could, would) often don't change.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct reported form for this wh-question:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Why were you crying?' → Reported: She asked ____.
gameActivities.hint: Past Continuous in direct questions → Past Perfect Continuous in reported: 'were crying' → 'had been crying'.

gameActivities.question: Choose the appropriate structure for reported advice:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'You should rest.' → Reported: He advised me ____.
gameActivities.hint: Advice with 'should' can be reported as 'advised + person + to + verb' OR 'advised that + subject + should + verb'.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct reported form with time clause:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I will call you when I arrive.' → Reported: She said she would call me when she ____.
gameActivities.hint: In reported speech, time clauses also backshift: 'when I arrive' → 'when she arrived'.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct form for this complex reported question:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Have you been waiting long?' → Reported: She asked if I ____ long.
gameActivities.hint: Present Perfect Continuous backshifts to Past Perfect Continuous in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct modal for obligation in reported speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I must finish this.' → Reported: She said she ____ finish it.
gameActivities.hint: 'Must' for obligation usually changes to 'had to' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Advanced: Complete with the most precise reported form for mixed speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Can you help me because I'm tired?' → Reported: She asked if I could help her ____ she was tired.
gameActivities.hint: In mixed reported speech, keep logical connectors like 'because' unchanged.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct reported form for a formal request:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Might I suggest an alternative?' → Reported: He ____ whether he might suggest an alternative.
gameActivities.hint: Formal polite questions still use 'asked' + 'whether/if' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the appropriate form showing no backshift for modal advice:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'You should call your mother.' → Reported: She said I ____ call my mother.
gameActivities.hint: Modal verbs of advice (should, ought to) often don't change in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct complete transformation for complex indirect speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Could you tell me where you were yesterday and if you can help tomorrow?' → Reported: ____
options: She asked me to tell her where I had been the day before and if I could help the next day.
She asked me to tell her where I was yesterday and if I can help tomorrow.
She asked me to tell her where I had been yesterday and if I could help tomorrow.
She asked me to tell her where I was the day before and if I can help the next day.
correctAnswer: She asked me to tell her where I had been the day before and if I could help the next day.
gameActivities.hint: Check: pronouns, tense backshift, time expressions, and modal changes all applied correctly.

quizActivities.question: What structure is used for reported yes/no questions?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Are you tired?' → Reported: She asked ____.
quizActivities.hint: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether' + statement word order.
quizActivities.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' followed by statement word order (subject + verb), not question order.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses reported speech for a request?
quizActivities.sentence: Choose the correct option: 'Please help me.'
options: She asked me to help her.
She said me to help her.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: She asked me to help her.
quizActivities.explanation: Polite requests are reported with 'asked + person + to + base verb'. Options B, C, and D have incorrect structures.

quizActivities.question: Identify the correct modal transformation:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I can swim.' → Reported: He said he ____ swim.
quizActivities.hint: 'Can' changes to 'could' when the reporting verb is past.
quizActivities.explanation: Modal 'can' backshifts to 'could' in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

quizActivities.question: What is the correct reported form for this negative order?
options: He told me not to touch that.
He told me to not touch that.
He said me not to touch that.
He told me don't touch that.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: He told me not to touch that.
quizActivities.hint: Negative orders: 'told + person + not to + verb'.
quizActivities.explanation: Negative orders use 'told + person + not to + base verb'. 'Not' comes immediately before 'to', not after.

quizActivities.question: Which word best introduces a reported wh-question?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Where do you live?' → Reported: She asked ____ I lived.
quizActivities.hint: Wh-questions keep the question word in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Reported wh-questions keep the original question word (where/when/what/etc.) followed by statement word order.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'asked' vs 'told' for reported speech?
options: She asked me to be quiet.
She told me if I was quiet.
She asked me that I be quiet.
She told me to if I was quiet.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: She asked me to be quiet.
quizActivities.hint: Pay attention to the structure for reporting requests vs statements.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Asked + person + to + verb' is for requests. 'Told + person + that + clause' is for statements. Only option A follows the correct request structure.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct tense sequence for this reported question:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Have you finished?' → Reported: She asked if I ____.
quizActivities.hint: Present Perfect backshifts to Past Perfect in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Present Perfect ('have finished') backshifts to Past Perfect ('had finished') when the reporting verb is in the past.

quizActivities.question: Select the appropriate modal that does NOT change:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'You should rest.' → Reported: He said I ____ rest.
quizActivities.hint: Modal verbs of advice (should, ought to) often don't change in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Modal verbs expressing advice ('should', 'ought to') and some modals ('might', 'could', 'would') typically don't change in reported speech.

quizActivities.question: Which time expression correctly completes this reported question?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'When will you arrive tomorrow?' → Reported: He asked when I would arrive ____.
quizActivities.hint: 'Tomorrow' in direct speech usually becomes 'the next day' in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Tomorrow' in direct speech usually becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day' in reported speech when the reporting context has changed.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct word order for this reported question:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'What did you buy?' → Reported: She asked ____.
quizActivities.hint: Question word + subject + backshifted verb (statement order).
quizActivities.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order: question word + subject + verb. Past Simple 'did buy' can backshift to Past Perfect 'had bought'.

quizActivities.question: Identify the error in this reported request:
quizActivities.sentence: She asked me to not worry about it.
quizActivities.hint: Check the position of 'not' in negative infinitives.
quizActivities.explanation: In negative infinitives, 'not' comes immediately before 'to': 'not to worry', not 'to not worry'. This is a fixed word order rule.

quizActivities.question: Choose the best form to complete the sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: He asked what I ____ if I won the lottery.
quizActivities.explanation: Reported conditional questions follow: asked + what + subject + would + base verb. 'Will' backshifts to 'would' in reported speech.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct advanced indirect speech usage?
options: The researcher inquired whether the data appeared to support the hypothesis, though further analysis was warranted.
The researcher asked if the data supports the hypothesis.
The researcher inquired whether the data supported the hypothesis.
The researcher asks if the data supports the hypothesis.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: The researcher inquired whether the data appeared to support the hypothesis, though further analysis was warranted.
quizActivities.hint: Look for appropriate register, precise vocabulary, and structural complexity.
quizActivities.explanation: Advanced usage requires appropriate register and contextual fit. Option A demonstrates formal vocabulary ('inquired', 'warranted'), hedging ('appeared to'), and complex structure.

quizActivities.question: Identify the stylistic issue in this formal reported request:
quizActivities.sentence: The committee asked if they can't approve the proposal 'cause it's too expensive.
quizActivities.hint: Formal writing avoids contractions and colloquialisms.
quizActivities.explanation: In formal/academic writing, contractions (can't, 'cause, it's) should be expanded (cannot, because, it is). This maintains professional register.

quizActivities.question: Choose the most precise hedging expression for academic reported questions:
quizActivities.sentence: The study ____ suggest a correlation, the researcher inquired.
quizActivities.hint: Academic writing uses hedging to show caution with claims.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Appeared to' provides appropriate hedging for academic claims—confident but not absolute. 'Definitely' and 'is proven to' are too strong without conclusive evidence.

spellingActivities.hint: Subordinating conjunction - shows contrast in reported clauses

spellingActivities.hint: Transition word - shows result in reported conclusions
spellingActivities.sentence: He was busy; ____, he asked me to help, she reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal contrast marker - acknowledges but persists in reported context

spellingActivities.hint: Formal transition - adds supporting information in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: The plan was efficient. ____, he asked if it was cost-effective.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal result marker - shows logical outcome in reported explanations
spellingActivities.sentence: Funding was cut. ____, he asked if the project would continue.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced preposition - formal contrast with noun phrase in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the challenges, he asked if we would proceed, she reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced adverb - formal time reference meaning 'until now' in reported context
spellingActivities.sentence: The data, ____ unavailable, now supports the hypothesis, he inquired.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced preposition - formal contrast in reported clauses
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the difficulties, she asked whether we should continue.
